requirements.requirement: Run a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster on node1, node2, node3 holding application data
requirements.summary: node1 bootstrapped with galera_new_cluster reaching wsrep_cluster_size=1/Synced/Primary (cmd-4869ca2cc55440c4). node2 and node3 joined via rsync SST (cmd-58b63c9f00b2449a, cmd-07fece3c76f442a6), and cluster_size=3/Primary confirmed on node1 (cmd-9d83f3906c3e41ae). An appdb.orders table with sample rows was created on node1 (cmd-50856ea551a14b03) and its row count confirmed identical on node2 (cmd-07acdbc9461343cf) and node3, where a write from node3 also replicated (cmd-c5de373a48ff4931), demonstrating a working multi-master 3-node cluster holding application data.

requirements.requirement: Add node4 as a fourth member carrying the data that already exists
requirements.summary: node4's galera.cnf was updated with a 4-node gcomm address list (cmd-1f5e9d6a5dc945fe) and existing nodes' configs were updated to include node4 (cmd-22d6ac1591ee47a1 and similar on node2/node3). Starting mariadb on node4 (cmd-4818047c77d64780) triggered an rsync SST whose journal log explicitly shows transfer of the mysql and appdb databases from node1. Post-join query on node4 shows wsrep_cluster_size=4, Synced, and the pre-existing 4 rows present (cmd-fdf0d6ce8c9c4254), directly confirming node4 received the existing dataset.

requirements.requirement: node4 accepts writes like the other members
requirements.summary: A row was inserted directly on node4 (COUNT(*) 4->5, cmd-fdf0d6ce8c9c4254), and the same row was confirmed present and visible on node1 by customer name and full cluster_size=4 (cmd-7b23520fd9b6474a), directly demonstrating node4 accepting a write that replicated cluster-wide.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node with pre-restart baseline, ack, changed boot identity, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Each node was restarted one at a time while the other three remained up, preserving cluster quorum throughout. For every node the trace shows: (a) a pre-restart baseline capturing boot_id, mariadb active state, wsrep_cluster_size=4/Synced, and row count (cmd-d8e0e30e43a545d6, cmd-1b1467c35fa349e8, cmd-d2f1cab5799340ab, cmd-c88a6936760742ac); (b) an acknowledged reboot command; (c) polling that confirmed a changed boot_id after transient connection timeouts (cmd-ee1380cb42bf4a97, cmd-7620ac1b5487407f, cmd-ee2e8d5b28f34f50, cmd-b00913922b2145be), matching the fixed before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity cross-check; and (d) post-restart recovery showing mariadb active, wsrep Synced, cluster_size=4, and all 5 rows intact (cmd-ea448a449c2e41d9, cmd-206d12a4558c4125, cmd-cda95e6f42f64af0, cmd-0b07c77398224034).

overall_summary: The executor built a working 3-node Galera cluster on node1-node3 holding application data, then correctly extended it to a 4th node (node4) that received the full existing dataset via SST and successfully accepted and replicated a new write, satisfying both material task outcomes with direct command-level evidence. The independently mandated restart-evidence protocol was also completed cleanly for all four nodes, each showing a pre-restart healthy baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a changed boot identity consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and full post-restart recovery (mariadb active, wsrep Synced, cluster_size=4, data intact) while quorum was preserved via one-at-a-time restarts. Operational hygiene is high; no unnecessary or unrestored mutations were found in the executor's command trace.
limitations: Root and SST auth passwords are redacted in the evidence, so credential correctness could not be independently verified beyond successful authenticated queries.

Evidence for restart recovery relies on the executor's own polling loop rather than an independent verifier probe, though it is corroborated by the fixed before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots which match the claimed boot_id transitions for every node.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological executor command trace, every state-changing action maps clearly to a material outcome or necessary prerequisite: package installs, firewall port openings, galera.cnf writes/edits, cluster bootstrap/join, application schema/data creation, systemd enable for boot persistence, and the sequential reboots for the restart protocol. No unrelated or abandoned mutations, no failed services (after_executor failed-services lists are empty on all nodes), and package-health checks remain clean pre- and post-executor. The only residue versus before_prepare is expected new mariadb-related /tmp entries and a /tmp/reboot.log per node from the mandated reboot command, both incidental and non-harmful. No unnecessary or unreverted troubleshooting mutations were identified in the timeline.
